atomic_facts.fact: Elizabeth Holmes was convicted of one count of conspiracy to commit wire fraud against investors.
She was convicted of three counts of wire fraud involving investments totaling more than $140 million.
These four counts constituted a conviction for defrauding investors.
Holmes was acquitted of a charge relating to patient-related conspiracy to commit wire fraud.
She was acquitted of three other wire fraud counts.
An additional charge of wire fraud related to a Theranos patient was dismissed during trial.
Overall, she was found not guilty on four counts of defrauding patients.
Holmes's original sentence was 135 months (11 years and 3 months).
In March 2026, a federal judge reduced her sentence to 123 months.
The reduction was granted as relief under a retroactive amendment addressing sentencing guidelines.
The Ninth Circuit rejected Holmes's appeal.
The Ninth Circuit upheld her conviction, sentence, and restitution order.
The appellate ruling upholding her conviction occurred in February 2025.
Walgreens settled a class-action lawsuit over Theranos blood tests.
The Theranos tests at issue were fraudulent.
If a judge approves the settlement, patients who bought a Theranos blood test would receive double the amount they paid for it.
